Capital One. What's in your wallet?
Terms apply. Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Homeland Security Secretary Mark Wayne Mullen says the communications problems
that led to the ongoing nationwide ground stop don't appear to be linked to the FAA's
new AI-powered system or any kind of terrorist attack.
Tom Lintner, the former head of air traffic investigations with the FAA,
has more on the last nationwide ground stop in 2023.
The NOTAM system, it's a communication system that provides information
back and forth between air traffic control facilities and pilots went out of service.
Out of an abundance of caution, the FAA restricted all departures for about 90 minutes
until that data was restored.
That, to my knowledge, was the only other time other than 9/11
when there was a nationwide ground stop.
The Trump administration is giving states another six months
before they must remove beneficiaries from Medicaid for failing to meet work requirements.
States have been scrambling to implement the requirement
that was part of President Trump's big tax and policy law
by January 1st, by the January 1st start date.
The administration says states still have to determine whether recipients are working,
going to school, or volunteering, but they can choose not to remove anyone from coverage for now.
Democratic victories in southern states have scrambled the map for the 2028 election,
and PR's Domenico Montanaro has more on whether this year's victories will have staying power.
This is a giant asterisk where a perfect storm of terrible national environment for Republicans,
good Democratic candidates who are able to capitalize and low Republican turnout made this possible.
Or is there a real path in the South for Democrats at the presidential level?
Now, I'm skeptical that Mississippi or South Carolina would be in that conversation long term,
given just how many Republicans there are there.
But Texas, with its 40 electoral votes and a diverse population,
whether that's going to be one that Democrats really seriously test out.
NPR's Domenico Montanaro reporting,
"A great rescue cruise in New Orleans had to pull passengers from the Mississippi River today
after an oil tanker struck a riverboat cruise liner,
and PR's Debbie Elliott reports at least 32 people are hospitalized, all with non-life-threatening injuries."
The tanker, called Atlantic Asphalt, struck the American Heritage Paddle Wheeler just after noon
as passengers were disembarking.
The impact quickly toppled and sank the cruise ship, sending people into the water.
New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno says police, firefighters, the Coast Guard, and nearby ships came to the rescue.
"We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi."
Video shows the tanker appearing to lose steerage after it navigated a sharp crescent turn in the Mississippi River at New Orleans.
The crash closed down river traffic for much of the day.
Debbie Elliott, NPR News.
Stocks fell and shaky trading on Wall Street today, but the market still posted its first winning week since early October.
This is NPR.
Ukraine launched nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets
in one of its largest aerial attacks since the war began five years ago.
This comes as negotiators discuss broader European security arrangements,
raising concerns among European leaders about NATO's future.
After two days of talks in Abu Dhabi this week, U.S. envoys briefed Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
A new report details the circumstances surrounding the deaths of four wildland firefighters
battling the blazes near the Colorado-Utah border in late June.
The Mountain West News Bureau's Murphy Woodhouse has more.
Faced with rapidly approaching flames, five wildland firefighters raced under their fire shelters for a shot at survival.
Three died there, and a fourth died a month later.
Federal investigators say extreme fire behavior, communication breakdowns, staffing shortages, and other issues led to the tragedy.
Former federal fire researcher Dave Kocken praised the report's detail, but said it failed to ask some key questions.
All of this complexity with that weather forecast suggested a need for somebody, for a system to save action is not feasible today.
The Department of Interior, which released the report, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Their recommendations include hiring and communications improvements.
For NPR News, I'm Murphy Woodhouse.
The U.S. flu season is off to a very early start, and it's quickly intensifying.
The CDC reports that seven states were reporting high flu activity last week, up from two the week before.
The surge began in the nation's south and west.
People should still get a flu shot if they haven't received one already.
This is NPR News.

Oil tanker Atlantic Asphalt strikes riverboat American Heritage on Mississippi River in New Orleans, sinking it
